preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 2 <= n <= 100 and isinstance(q, int) and 1 <= q <= 100 for n, q in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is between 2 and 100, and q is between 1 and 100.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == n and all(c in '01' for c in s) for s in strings)
preconditions.description: Each string s has length n and contains only '0' and '1'.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= l < r <= n for l, r in queries)
preconditions.description: For each query, 1 <= l < r <= n.

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines) == sum(q for _, q, _, _ in test_cases)
postconditions.description: The total number of output lines equals the sum of q over all test cases.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[idx] == 'YES' or output_lines[idx] == 'NO') for idx in range(len(output_lines)))
postconditions.description: Each output line is either 'YES' or 'NO' (case-insensitive allowed, but normalized to uppercase for checking).

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[idx] == 'YES') == exists_good_subsequence(s, l, r) for idx, (s, l, r) in enumerate(query_iterator))
postconditions.description: For each query (l, r) on string s, the output is 'YES' if and only if there exists a good subsequence of s equal to the substring s[l...r].
